surface_mechanism_description: During PE-ALD, NH3 plasma reacts with metal precursors to form metallic materials, while SiH4 species form SiNx by reacting with NH3. A submonolayer of SiNx prevents lateral growth of Co islands, leading to NR formation. The SiNx layer aggregates to the sidewalls, exposing only the top of the NRs for further deposition. Plasma bombardment may also contribute to NR formation by removing the top of the NR while preserving the SiNx layer on the sidewalls.
evidence: During the plasma exposure step, NH3 species in the plasma mixture react with metal precursors to form metallic materials, while SiH4 species do not contribute to the deposition. Instead, they have a tendency to form the SiNx phase by reacting with NH3 species. At a suitable rate of SiH4 flow, a submonolayer of SiNx is formed during the plasma exposure step. The SiNx layer either prevents the lateral growth of Co or coalescence of Co islands. The Co and SiNx do not mix with each other and the SiNx layer aggregates to the sidewalls, thus exposing only the top of the NRs for further deposition. Bombarding effects caused by the plasma may also contribute to the formation of NRs. When the SiNx is formed during the plasma exposure step, the top of the NR is bombarded away while the SiNx layer formed at the sidewall remains intact.
